sections.title: Market Pulse: Tech-Led Rally Amid Inflation Concerns

items.headline: U.S. Equities Advance, Driven by Strong Tech Earnings Despite Inflation Data
items.summary: U.S. stock markets closed higher on August 27, 2026, with major indices showing a volatile rebound. Technology stocks led the gains following impressive earnings reports from NVIDIA and other software companies, which overshadowed persistent inflation concerns highlighted by the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index. Investors also focused on the ongoing Federal Reserve's Jackson Hole Symposium for future policy signals.

items.headline: NVIDIA Shares Surge on Blowout Earnings and Upbeat Guidance
items.summary: NVIDIA ($NVDA) climbed 8.74% to $227.98 after reporting second-quarter revenue that more than doubled year-over-year to $96.2 billion, significantly beating expectations. The chipmaker also provided a strong revenue outlook for the third quarter, easing concerns about a potential slowdown in the AI industry.

items.headline: Okta Jumps on Strong Q2 Results and Raised Outlook
items.summary: Okta ($OKTA) surged 24% after the identity and access management company reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.05, exceeding estimates, and revenue rose 11% year-over-year to $805 million. The company also raised its FY2027 outlook, with strong demand linked to agentic AI cited as a key driver.

items.headline: Salesforce Rallies on Strong Q2 Performance and AI-Related Demand
items.summary: Salesforce ($CRM) jumped 20% following robust Q2 results, with revenue increasing 11% year-over-year. The enterprise software giant benefited from strong AI-related demand, with AI and data products' Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) nearing $4 billion, and a new partnership with Anthropic.

items.headline: CrowdStrike Climbs on Upbeat Q2 Results and AI Adoption
items.summary: CrowdStrike ($CRWD) advanced 19% after the cybersecurity company reported strong Q2 results, with ARR rising 25% to $5.84 billion. The company also raised its FY2027 revenue guidance, driven by accelerating AI adoption and the increasing need for secure AI-driven enterprise environments.

items.headline: HP Slips on Weak PC Shipments Despite Q3 Beat
items.summary: HP ($HPQ) closed down 2.93% at $29.62. Investors focused on weak PC shipment trends and margin pressure from higher memory and commodity costs, even though the company reported stronger-than-expected Q3 sales and adjusted EPS growth.

items.headline: Moderna Weakens as Revenue Decline Weighs on Performance
items.summary: Moderna ($MRNA) was among the weakest performers, returning -5.8%. The company's revenue declined 27.7% over the last twelve months, contributing to the negative sentiment.

items.headline: Expedia Leads Declines Among Travel Stocks
items.summary: Expedia ($EXPE) led decliners at just under 5%. Other travel and entertainment related stocks like Spotify ($SPOT), iQIYI ($IQ), and fuboTV ($FUBO) also traded lower.

items.headline: Elevated PCE Index Fuels Inflation Concerns, Pressuring Consumer Sentiment
items.summary: The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose 0.2% sequentially in July, bringing the annual inflation rate to 3.7%. Both annual and monthly readings surpassed analysts' expectations, contributing to investors' dampened confidence and suggesting that policymakers may consider further rate hikes.

items.headline: Jackson Hole Symposium Commences with Focus on Fed Chair's Speech
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's annual symposium in Jackson Hole began on August 27, 2026, with investors closely watching for insights from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's upcoming speech. Expectations around Fed policy, particularly regarding interest rates, remain a significant market driver.

items.headline: Technology Sector Leads Market Gains; Consumer Staples Lag
items.summary: The Information Technology sector was the top-performing sector on August 27, 2026, driven by strong earnings from chipmakers and software companies, with a gain of 3.40%. In contrast, the Consumer Staples sector was the worst-performing, losing 1.50%. The energy sector also performed weakly due to falling international oil prices.

items.headline: Best Buy Beats Q2 Expectations and Raises Full-Year Guidance
items.summary: Best Buy ($BBY) announced strong results for its second quarter, with comparable sales increasing 4.1% and adjusted diluted EPS up 15% to $1.47. The company raised its FY27 comparable sales guidance to 1.9% to 3.0% and adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $6.70 to $6.90, driven by growth across most product categories.

items.headline: Gap Inc. Reports Mixed Q2 Results, Exceeding Profit but Sales Modestly Below Expectations
items.summary: Gap Inc. ($GPS) reported second-quarter fiscal 2026 results with net sales down 2% and comparable sales down 1% year-over-year. However, the company exceeded profit expectations due to strong gross margin, driven by a significant adjustment related to IEEPA tariff recovery.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Reports Record Q2 Revenue, Guides Strong for Q3
items.summary: Marvell Technology ($MRVL) reported record Q2 net revenue of $2.739 billion, a 37% year-over-year increase, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.94. The company also provided strong guidance for Q3, projecting net revenue of $3.150 billion (±5%) and non-GAAP diluted net income per share of $1.10 (±$0.05).
